answers.answer: In the 3-player case, the tied leaders gain nothing and the uniquely last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “unique leader gains 1 coin; a tied lead gives no coin”; “In a 2-player game the last player never pays”.

answers.answer: No. You may draw at most two because only two Market spaces are free, and you are not required to draw the full allowance. Unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: draw “any number up to” allowance, “limited by free Market spaces”; unused Market Followers remain and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: You may fill an action over multiple rounds, but cannot execute it until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall has its exception). You may save an activated action for a later round. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology stays on its spaces.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “fill an action gradually over multiple rounds”; activation requires all spaces; “An activation can be saved”; after ordinary action Followers return to bag.

answers.answer: Starting with Start Player and proceeding clockwise, players take one activated action or pass on each turn. Passing ends your participation for the round; you cannot act later, and any unused activation keeps its Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “one activated action or passing”; passing “ends your participation”; unused activations keep Followers for future rounds.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted at that track space.

Village recruits one of a Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader into your bag and advances that profession’s track. Boatman gives the depicted coins (or a Citizen at the last space to the first player there); Craftsman gives a Technology tile; Trader gives a Place Tile, with the first Trader advance limited to category I and later advances allowing category I or II.

No. A Craftsman’s Technology can be used only after you pass, so it cannot help another action that round after that pass. The first Technology must replace a Farmer. Later Technology may replace any profession except Monk; no Place may have more than one Technology, and no Technology may go on a Place requiring only one Follower.
On the first Trader-track advance, only category I is allowed. On every later advance, category I or II is allowed. Players may inspect the stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment; Setup, Place Tile stacks.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track, and grants its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances the Knights Track; the track sets future draw allowance. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. The fourth Knight leaves allowance at 7 and gives its Citizen to the first player there. Once a character track is at its last space, that corresponding action cannot be taken again.
answers.evidence: Actions table; Castle rewards; Character-track limits.

answers.answer: A Monk may replace any profession on ordinary actions. No other Follower or Technology can replace a required Monk. Monks and other substitutions cannot replace the exact professions printed on Beneficial Deed spaces.
answers.evidence: Monks; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Ship moves the Merchant one adjacent town along one Waterway; Wagon moves it one adjacent town along one Road. You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if several are there; taking it is optional. An empty connection is legal and yields no good.
Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the Merchant’s current town. A town with any player’s station cannot receive another; the exception is Orléans, where each player may build one station.

Scriptorium gives 1 Development Point. Moving onto or past a coin space gives its depicted coins; the first player onto/past a Citizen space takes that Citizen; reaching or passing a Development Status space immediately changes Status to its shown value.

Town Hall works with one or two eligible neutral Followers; one or both may be sent in one action. Your marked starting Followers cannot be used. Send them permanently to free Deed spaces matching their exact professions; take each depicted coin reward, or for Canalization choose 1 coin or 1 Development Point. Whoever fills a Deed’s last space takes its Citizen.
Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment during the round’s Action Phase, before the Phase 6 event. Other events resolve in Phase 6. The setup places Pilgrimage on top, so it opens the game.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Events; Setup, Hour Glass stack.

answers.answer: Harvest accepts grain, cheese, or wine, returned to the Goods Market; wool and brocade do not qualify. If you cannot pay food, pay 5 coins instead; if you cannot pay those coins, undergo torture for the shortfall.

A neutral Scholar is returned to its game-board supply and becomes recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. A marked starting Trader stays with you, and you lose no Follower that round; do not redraw.

Pay the available coin and replace each missing coin with one item, in any mix: a built or unbuilt Trading Station, a random eligible Follower drawn only from your bag, one Development Point moved left (never onto or past a coin space), one Goods Tile, one Place Tile, or one Technology tile. Market/Action Space Followers are ineligible. Marked starting Followers are returned and redrawn until an eligible neutral one is drawn; they cannot be surrendered. Items given up are removed from the game.

You cannot take an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part of it would give a reward. It becomes available again when the required tile returns to supply, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply is insufficient, players cannot receive coins at that moment.

A tie for most built Trading Stations means nobody receives the set-aside Citizen. At game end grain/cheese/wine/wool/brocade are worth 1/2/3/4/5 points each; coins are 1 each; score (built stations + collected Citizens) × final Development Status. Highest total wins; ties go to the player furthest along the Development Track, then are shared if still tied.

Each player takes a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Put the starting Followers on your Market, Merchant in Orléans, one marker on the first space of each of six Character Tracks and the Development Track, and keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. Youngest player takes the Start Player token.

Place 13 Citizens on their marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Sort neutral Followers by profession into their buildings, Technology into its supply, and coins nearby. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II. For four players, shuffle goods face down and deal one face up to each eligible Road/Waterway goods space, filling every such space; sort remaining goods face up into the Goods Market.

For 3 players remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders each; 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks each; and 6 random goods, leaving spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players remove 4 of each of the first four neutral professions; 6 of each Knight, Scholar, and Monk; and 12 random goods, leaving spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
Scriptorium: Knight + Scholar. Town Hall accepts 1 or 2 eligible Followers; for its Deed placement they must match the exact professions depicted on free Deed spaces.
answers.evidence: Actions required Followers table; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Yes. For each draw declined, you may move one Follower from an Action Space back to your Market. You cannot move a Follower directly from one Action Space to another.
Yes. You may inspect your bag at any time, but must shuffle its contents afterward.

The phases are Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. Pass Start Player to the player on your left. Planning begins simultaneously; if order matters, use clockwise order from Start Player. Payments and necessary order-sensitive event resolution proceed clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to the common supply; received coins come from it.
Do not score immediately. Finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including its event, then score.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “Finish the entire round…”

answers.answer: The uniquely leading player on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin; Farmer tiles in bags do not affect the comparison.
Income pays coins equal to your current Development Status.
Eight goods means two complete groups of three, so pay 2 coins. Goods types do not matter because all goods are counted. If you cannot pay, the shortfall causes torture.
answers.evidence: Events: Taxes: count all goods and pay 1 coin per complete group of 3 (round down); shortfall causes torture.

answers.answer: You receive 4 coins, one per built Trading Station; unbuilt stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Events: Trading Day; Building says only built stations count for income and final scoring.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer; take 1 grain from Goods Market. Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer; take 1 cheese from Goods Market. Winery: Farmer + Trader; take 1 wine from Goods Market. Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader; take 1 wool from Goods Market. Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader; take 1 brocade from Goods Market. A goods-producing Place cannot be used if its particular good is absent from the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table; goods availability rule.

answers.answer: Shipping Line (Boatman): gain 1 Development Point. Brewery (Monk): gain 2 coins. Windmill (Craftsman + Craftsman): gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library (Knight + Scholar): gain 2 Development Points.
Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins, advancing one Development space per coin paid; paying two advances two spaces. Zero and four coins are outside the allowed range.
Cellar (Monk + Scholar) gives 4 coins. Office (Scholar + Scholar) gives 1 coin per Trading Station you have built. Hospital (Boatman + Scholar) gives coins equal to your current Development Status.
Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight. It moves along one Road to an adjacent town and collects one good if available.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table: Horse Wagon.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile, subject to usual placement constraints. Your first Technology cannot be placed there because it must replace a Farmer. A later one can go on either Laboratory space if none is already there and usual constraints are met.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table: Laboratory; Technology rules.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires a Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces; neither may go on Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Farmer to your bag.

Place the one drawn Follower that can legally fit on an allowed Action Space. Return all other drawn Followers and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table: Bathhouse: if only one or none can legally be placed, do so and return all other drawn Followers to the bag.

answers.answer: The summary says Bathhouse places its chosen Followers immediately on Action Spaces, and Phase 5 allows taking one activated action per action turn. This supports using the newly completed Place on a later action turn in the same phase if you have not passed, though the summary does not state that specific timing ruling explicitly.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse: “immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces”; Turn Structure: in Actions take “one activated action” per turn and choose action order freely.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 you may return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague.
No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5, while Sacristy protection is used in Phase 6, so the later protection does not remove the earlier restriction.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Events: Pilgrimage; Sacristy timing.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not allow replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table: Herb Garden.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It requires no activation. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
No. Beneficial Deed spaces require the exact depicted professions, and substitutions cannot replace them. Using Gunpowder Tower does not change that rule.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds; Gunpowder Tower rules.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3 place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. During Planning move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, during Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in a single action. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent, and Deed spaces still require exact professions.
answers.evidence: 20 base Place Tiles table: Gunpowder Tower.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two tied for last pay nothing because a tied last place pays nothing.
The player with the unique most built Trading Stations receives the set-aside Citizen after completing the entire round 18 and before scoring. It counts among collected Citizens in final scoring.
Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, and put the lighter Pilgrimage on top. In Phase 1 the Start Player reveals the top tile.
Each remaining coin is worth 1 victory point.
Development Status starts at 1 and initial draw allowance is 4.
Only lost Development Points can be regained. Goods, Followers, Trading Stations, Places, and Technology surrendered to torture are removed from the game rather than returned to supplies.
You may choose the execution order of your activated actions freely.
Its passive ability is available immediately, including during the current Action Phase.
You may send just one, or both, in the Town Hall action; sending both is not required.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: “send one or both”.

answers.answer: You may complete the move and leave the good there; the summary says you may take one good, not that you must.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: “You may take one good”; empty connections are legal.

answers.answer: You may send the second Follower on a later action turn in the same Action Phase before passing; the two transfers need not occur in one action.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: “You may send its two Followers in separate action turns during the same Action Phase, before you pass.”
